translations.literal: Unless there were the tyranny of Jie and Zhou or the benevolence of Tang and Wu, with the people turning to them and Heaven ordaining them, the distinction of ruler and minister should be kept by holding to one's station and dying in submission—that is all.

sentences.zh: 然二子寧亡國而不為者，誠以禮之大節不可亂也。

translations.literal: Yet those two men would rather see their states perish than do it—truly because the great nodes of ritual must not be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those two men would rather see their states perish than do it—truly because the great nodes of ritual must not be disturbed.

translations.literal: Hence it is said: Among ritual none is greater than distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: Among ritual none is greater than distinction.

sentences.zh: ::夫禮，辨貴賤，序親疏，裁群物，制庶事。

translations.literal: :: Now ritual distinguishes noble and base, orders kin near and far, trims the myriad things, and regulates the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual distinguishes noble and base, orders kin near and far, trims the myriad things, and regulates the multitude of affairs.

translations.literal: Without naming, nothing is made known; without vessels, nothing takes form.
translations.idiomatic: Without naming, nothing is made known; without vessels, nothing takes form.

sentences.zh: 名以命之，器以別之，然後上下粲然有倫，此禮之大經也。

translations.literal: Names command things; vessels distinguish them—only then are high and low brilliantly ordered: this is the great warp of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Names command things; vessels distinguish them—only then are high and low brilliantly ordered: this is the great warp of ritual.

sentences.zh: 名器既亡，則禮安得獨在哉？

translations.literal: When names and vessels are lost, how can ritual alone remain?
translations.idiomatic: When names and vessels are lost, how can ritual alone remain?

sentences.zh: 昔仲叔於奚有功於衛，辭邑而請繁纓，孔子以為不如多與之邑。

translations.literal: Of old Zhongsun Yuxi had merit in Wei; he declined a town and asked for the grand tassel. Confucius thought it better to give him more towns.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Zhongsun Yuxi had merit in Wei; he declined a fief and asked for the grand tassel. Confucius thought it better to give him more towns.

sentences.zh: 惟器與名，不可以假人，君之所司也。

translations.literal: "Vessels and names may not be lent to others"—these are what the ruler oversees.
translations.idiomatic: "Vessels and names may not be lent to others"—these are what the ruler oversees.

translations.literal: When government perishes, the state follows.
translations.idiomatic: When government perishes, the state follows.

sentences.zh: 衛君待孔子而為政，孔子欲先正名，以為名不正則民無所措手足。

translations.literal: The lord of Wei waited on Confucius to govern; Confucius wished first to rectify names, holding that if names are not rectified the people have nowhere to set hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: The lord of Wei waited on Confucius to govern; Confucius wished first to rectify names, holding that if names are not rectified the people have nowhere to set hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 夫繁纓，小物也，而孔子惜之；

translations.literal: The grand tassel is a small thing, yet Confucius cherished it;
translations.idiomatic: The grand tassel is a small thing, yet Confucius cherished it;

sentences.zh: 正名，細務也，而孔子先之。

translations.literal: rectifying names is a fine matter, yet Confucius put it first.
translations.idiomatic: rectifying names is a fine matter, yet Confucius put it first.

sentences.zh: 誠以名器既亂，則上下無以相有故也。

translations.literal: Truly, once names and vessels are in disorder, high and low have no way to possess one another.
translations.idiomatic: Truly, once names and vessels are in disorder, high and low have no way to possess one another.

sentences.zh: 夫事未有不生於微而成於著。

translations.literal: Nothing arises that does not begin in the minute and come to completion in the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing arises that does not begin in the minute and come to completion in the manifest.

sentences.zh: 聖人之慮遠，故能謹其微而治之；

translations.literal: The sage's thought is far-reaching, and so he can be strict with the minute and govern it;
translations.idiomatic: The sage's thought is far-reaching, and so he can be strict with the minute and govern it;

sentences.zh: 眾人之識近，故必待其著而後救之。

translations.literal: the multitude's knowledge is near, and so they must wait until it is manifest and only then rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary men's knowledge is near, and so they must wait until trouble is manifest and only then rescue it.

sentences.zh: 治其微，則用力寡而功多；

translations.literal: To govern the minute, effort is little and achievement great;
translations.idiomatic: To govern the minute, effort is little and achievement great;

sentences.zh: 救其著，則竭力而不能及也。

translations.literal: to rescue the manifest, one exhausts strength yet cannot reach success.
translations.idiomatic: to rescue the manifest, one exhausts strength yet cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「履霜，堅冰至」，《書》曰：「一日二日萬幾」，謂此類也。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Treading frost, hard ice comes"; the Documents says, "In one day, two days, ten thousand affairs"—it speaks of this kind of thing.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "Treading frost, hard ice comes"; the Documents says, "In one day, two days, ten thousand affairs"—it speaks of this kind of thing.

translations.literal: Some may think that at that time the Zhou house was weak and the Three Jin strong—though one wished not to permit it, how could one obtain that?
translations.idiomatic: Some may think that at that time the Zhou house was weak and the Three Jin strong—though one wished not to permit it, how could one obtain that?

translations.idiomatic: This is greatly mistaken.

translations.literal: Though the Three Jin were strong, if they did not heed punishment from All-under-Heaven and violated righteousness and encroached on ritual, they would have set themselves up without asking the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Three Jin were strong, if they did not heed punishment from All-under-Heaven and violated righteousness and encroached on ritual, they would have set themselves up without asking the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 不請於天子而自立，則為悖逆之臣。

translations.literal: To set themselves up without asking the Son of Heaven would make them rebellious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: To set themselves up without asking the Son of Heaven would make them rebellious ministers.

sentences.zh: 天下苟有桓、文之君，必奉禮義而征之。

translations.literal: If All-under-Heaven had a lord like Duke Huan or Duke Wen, he would surely uphold ritual and righteousness and campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: If All-under-Heaven had a lord like Duke Huan or Duke Wen, he would surely uphold ritual and righteousness and campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 今請於天子而天子許之，是受天子之命而為諸侯也，誰得而討之！

translations.literal: Now they asked the Son of Heaven and the Son of Heaven permitted it—they received the Son of Heaven's command and became feudal lords: who could punish them!
translations.idiomatic: Now they asked the Son of Heaven and the Son of Heaven permitted it—they received the Son of Heaven's command and became feudal lords: who could punish them!

sentences.zh: 故三晉之列於諸侯，非三晉之壞禮，乃天子自壞之也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Three Jin's listing among the feudal lords was not the Three Jin destroying ritual—it was the Son of Heaven destroying it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Three Jin's listing among the feudal lords was not the Three Jin destroying ritual—it was the Son of Heaven destroying it himself.
